winner.title: Uzbek Lagman (Lamb Noodle Soup)

evidence.authenticity: Tomato-forward soup-style lagman with lamb, radish/turnip, celery, carrot, red pepper, kala jeera and star anise, served over noodles cooked separately. Author explains the lamian origin, the thicker Uzbek noodle, and a Los Angeles Uzbek restaurant and Riga versions. Author is not Uzbek and the noodles are store-bought fresh wheat noodles, not hand-pulled.
evidence.precision: Volumes for most ingredients (1 lb meat, 4 large tomatoes or a 28-oz can, 2 to 3 qt water, 'cover by about an inch'); 5-quart pot named. Oil amount is 'a bit'. Doneness cues are limited to browned meat, softened tomatoes and fragrant spices, plus a 30 to 45 minute simmer. Kala jeera is listed twice. No weights.
evidence.testing: Blogger-tested, with reasoning: kala jeera gives the smoky flavor and regular cumin is a poor substitute; lamb can be gamey so use leaner cuts. Not a test kitchen.
evidence.photos: WebFetch: 17 photos, 15 of them numbered step photos covering the recipe stages. The page has no Recipe schema.
evidence.efficiency: Noodles boil while the soup simmers. About 1 hr total with no wasted steps.
evidence.access: Kala jeera is hard to find, though the page says to seek it out and does not give a substitute for it. Udon or fettuccine is suggested for the noodles. Everything else is at a normal US grocery.

winner.why: It has the most step photos, real regional context and an explained spice choice, where the runner-up gives a thin explanation and no pan size.

runnerUp.title: Uzbek Lagman

evidence.authenticity: Soup-style Uzbek lagman with beef, potato, carrot, tomato, coriander, cumin and star anise over linguine. Uses pasta, not pulled noodles.
evidence.precision: Volumes given, but 'beef' has no weight beyond 1 lb and there are no pan size or doneness cues beyond 'tender'. 2 of 17 ingredients have weights.
evidence.testing: Home cook, rated 5 from 11 ratings, little reasoning.
evidence.photos: Page has many images, but the structured data lists no step images and I did not confirm process photos.

runnerUp.why: A fast, accessible weeknight version, but it is less authentic and less documented than the winner.

candidates.disqualified: Kazakh/Uyghur dry noodles with sauce, not the Uzbek soup-style dish.
Uyghur chopped lagman with soy sauce and frozen peas; fusion, not the dish.
Looks like an AI-generated content farm: generic text, 'Silas's definitive recipe', 1 rating.

notes: Sites search found nothing on Serious Eats, NYT, ATK or BBC. The winner is only just over 60, so a better source may exist. No English recipe I read makes traditional pulled chuzma noodles and a soup-style Uzbek lagman together, with weights and photos. Food Network's Nargis Cafe recipe is the most traditional but has implausible quantities (3 lb beef plus 3 lb lamb for 4 servings, 4 tbsp ground star anise) and no photos. Its cookingchanneltv.com URL redirects to a landing page, so only the foodnetwork.com URL was usable. The Wandering Chopsticks page has no Recipe structured data and was read with WebFetch. A Euronews video lesson (chef Bahriddin Chustiy) turned up in search but is video only and was not scored.
